hecate.name: Hecate
hecate.wordsLine: Hecate is one of the presiding deities of Sarvakali, and this pillar is under her keeping.
hecate.wordsNote: In Sarvakali’s words · a placeholder until Sarvakali writes these lines

supper.title: The dark moon is hers
supper.text: In ancient Athens the last day of the lunar month, the dark moon, belonged to Hecate. Households set out a supper for her and the restless dead, at crossroads and on doorsteps: the Deipnon. The same dark moon is Amavasya, a night especially kept for Kali.
supper.note: The Athenian month began with the first sliver of the new moon, so the old reckoning can differ from a modern calendar by a day. The two traditions are separate; here they simply share a night.
supper.calendar: Add the next three to your calendar

hecate.also: Hecate also stands among [the Greek gods, in Devotion](/pillars/devotion#the-greek-gods), and watches over the doorways in [Protection](#protection-cleansing-and-uncrossing).

sigil.title: Make a sigil
sigil.lede: Write what you wish for in a few words, then choose a way to turn it into a sigil. The same words give a different shape each way, and you can finish any of them by hand.

wheel.name: Letter wheel
wheel.how: The alphabet is set round a circle. The line starts with a small ring on the first letter, runs from letter to letter, and ends with a short bar.
wheel.origin: A modern way of tracing a name on letters set in a ring. The Golden Dawn’s Rose Cross, whose 22 petals carry the Hebrew letters, was called the key of sigils.

monogram.name: Monogram
monogram.how: The letters that repeat are struck out, and many modern versions drop the vowels too. What is left is joined into one figure: hung on a central line, set around a ring, or stacked. Then move, turn or flip any letter until it feels right.
monogram.origin: The way made known by the artist Austin Osman Spare in The Book of Pleasure (1913), and taken up by chaos magic.

square.name: Magic square
square.how: Each letter becomes a number (A to I count 1 to 9, then J starts again at 1). The numbers are found on the square and joined in order.
square.origin: Old seals of spirits were drawn this way, on number squares. This is the 3 × 3 square, which Agrippa gave to Saturn; counting Latin letters 1 to 9 is a modern adaptation.

bindrune.name: Bindrune
bindrune.how: The first letter of each word becomes its nearest Elder Futhark rune, and the runes are bound onto one shared stave.
bindrune.origin: Runes joined into one figure appear in old inscriptions, some along a single stave. Making one from your own words is a modern use of that old form.

draw.name: Draw your own
draw.how: No letters and no rule: draw whatever shape comes to you.
draw.origin: No tradition is claimed here: a free drawing.

sigil.note: Sarvakali may make sigils differently. Nothing you type or draw here is saved or sent.
sigil.placeholder: Your intention, in a few words
sigil.hint: Your sigil will be drawn here.

love.title: Love, attraction and glamour
love.line: Calling love in, mending what can be mended, letting go of what cannot, and learning to love yourself.

abundance.title: Abundance, career and success
abundance.line: Money, work, clients and luck: opening the road and keeping it open.

protection.title: Protection, cleansing and uncrossing
protection.line: Shielding you and your home, clearing what clings, and lifting what was laid on you.

baneful.title: Baneful and dark craft
baneful.line: Binding, justice and the older, darker arts, held with discernment.

spellcraft.title: Spellcraft and magical objects
spellcraft.line: Candles, jars, sigils, talismans, oils and the old folk ways: spells made by hand, for you.

rituals.title: Rituals, ceremonies and paths
rituals.line: Ceremony, fire and the four directions, rites of passage, and the many paths of the craft.

nature.title: Nature, moon and cosmic magic
nature.line: The moon and the planets, the turning year, herbs, stones and the wild places.

protectionKeeper: Hecate, honoured of old at crossroads and doorways, keeps watch over this chapter, and over the home and threshold work in it.
banefulCare: Baneful work is considered case by case and may be declined. [Read Boundaries and care](/care).

wheel.hint: Drag to turn the wheel. The marker at the top is today.

samhain.name: Samhain
samhain.line: The dark half of the year begins; a time to honour the dead

yule.name: Yule
yule.line: The winter solstice: the longest night, and the light’s return

imbolc.name: Imbolc
imbolc.line: The first stirrings of spring; associated with Brigid

ostara.name: Ostara
ostara.line: The spring equinox: day and night in balance

beltane.name: Beltane
beltane.line: The start of summer: fire, fertility and bloom

litha.name: Litha
litha.line: The summer solstice: the longest day

lughnasadh.name: Lughnasadh
lughnasadh.line: The first harvest, named for the god Lugh

mabon.name: Mabon
mabon.line: The autumn equinox: balance again, and the second harvest

close.title: Every spell begins with an intention
close.lede: Tell Sarvakali what you would like to change. Together you will find the right working.
